Identify: - Core topic - Primary message - User intent - Important arguments The rewritten article MUST preserve these elements. Your task is to optimize—not replace—the original article. --- ## 3. KEYWORD RESEARCH Analyze the article together with your research. ### Primary Keyword Select ONE primary keyword. Requirements: - Highly relevant. - Strong SEO potential. - Matches user intent. - Fits naturally into the article. ### Supporting Keywords Generate FOUR additional SEO-friendly keywords. Requirements: - Relevant to the article. - Support the primary keyword. - Cover related search intent. - Suitable for evergreen SEO. ### Uniqueness Constraint (Critical) Compare every candidate keyword against: `old_keyword` All FIVE generated keywords MUST: - Be completely new. - Be significantly different. - Not be synonyms. - Not be close variants. - Not be stem/root/plural/singular versions. - Not overlap with any keyword in `old_keyword`. The first keyword in the array becomes the primary keyword. --- ## 4. TITLE OPTIMIZATION Rewrite the title. Requirements: - Begin with the exact primary keyword. - Maximum 60 characters. - Evergreen. - SEO-friendly. - Match the rewritten article. ### Sentence Case The title MUST follow sentence case. Rules: - Capitalize only the first word. - Capitalize proper nouns. - Everything else lowercase. Correct: ``` Expense tracking for small businesses ``` Incorrect: ``` Expense Tracking For Small Businesses expense tracking for small businesses ``` ### Existing Title Constraint Compare against: `existing_title` The generated title MUST have zero lexical overlap. Do NOT reuse: - Words - Roots - Stems - Derivatives - Singular/plural forms - Abbreviations - Close variations --- ## 5. CONTENT OPTIMIZATION Rewrite the article. Preserve: - Core message. - User intent. - Primary arguments. Improve: - SEO - Readability - Structure - Authority - Engagement The rewritten article must feel like an improved version of the original—not an entirely different article. --- ### Writing Quality (Highest Priority) The article must sound natural and human. #### Structural Variety (Critical) Never produce repetitive writing. Forbidden: - Consecutive sentences starting with the same word. - Repeated sentence patterns. - Mechanical paragraph structures. Every paragraph should read naturally. --- ### Active Voice Write primarily using active voice. Passive voice should represent less than 10% of all sentences. --- ### Paragraph Length Each paragraph must contain no more than 150 words. --- ### Flow Use natural transitions between: - Sentences - Paragraphs - Sections Ensure the article feels cohesive. --- ### Content Length The rewritten article MUST contain at least **1000 words**. Use Gemini Search to enrich the article with: - Better explanations - Examples - Practical guidance - Supporting facts Present everything in an evergreen manner. --- ### Keyword Integration The primary keyword MUST: - Appear naturally at least 5 times. - Appear in the first paragraph. - Be distributed organically. - Never be stuffed. The remaining four keywords should also appear naturally throughout the article where appropriate. --- ### Heading Structure Use multiple headings. Allowed: ```

``` Requirements: - Most headings should contain the primary keyword. - Every heading MUST use sentence case. Do NOT generate any `

`. --- ### Internal Linking Review the supplied `related` array. Select one or two highly relevant articles. Insert natural internal links using: ```html Anchor text ``` Anchor text should describe the destination naturally. --- ### Outbound Linking Use Gemini Search to identify ONE authoritative external resource. Requirements: - Directly relevant. - Highly authoritative. - Publicly accessible. - Canonical URL. - HTTPS only. - URL must resolve correctly. Insert one natural outbound link: ```html Anchor text ``` The link should genuinely help the reader. --- ### HTML Formatting Return the content as HTML. Allowed tags include: ```

    ``` --- ## 6. META DESCRIPTION Generate an SEO-friendly meta description. Requirements: - Maximum 140 characters. - Naturally include the primary keyword. - Match the rewritten article. - Encourage clicks. - Written in the detected language. --- ## 7. FINAL OUTPUT Assemble the results into ONE JSON object. The JSON MUST contain exactly these keys: ```json { "title": "", "content": "", "keywords": [ "", "", "", "", "" ], "meta_description": "" } ``` Requirements for `keywords`: - Must be a JSON array. - Must contain exactly **5** keywords. - The first keyword is the primary keyword. - The remaining four are supporting SEO keywords. - Every keyword must be unique. No additional keys are allowed. --- # OUTPUT CONTRACT (CRITICAL) Your response MUST consist ONLY of the final JSON object. DO NOT output: - Any introduction - Any explanation - Any reasoning - Any confirmation - Any notes - Any apologies - Any Markdown - Any headings - Any bullet lists - Any code fences - Any text before the JSON - Any text after the JSON Forbidden examples include: - "Certainly!" - "Here is the optimized article." - "Below is the JSON." - "I've completed the optimization." - "Based on my research..." The FIRST character of your response MUST be: ``` { ``` The LAST character of your response MUST be: ``` } ``` The output MUST be valid JSON that can be parsed directly using `JSON.parse()` without any preprocessing. If any requested content cannot be generated, you MUST still return a valid JSON object following the required schema. Never explain the issue outside the JSON. --- # EXECUTION COMMAND Execute every step above in the specified order. Return ONLY the following JSON object. ```json { "title": "Optimized title", "content": "

    Optimized HTML article...

    ", "keywords": [ "Primary keyword", "Supporting keyword 1", "Supporting keyword 2", "Supporting keyword 3", "Supporting keyword 4" ], "meta_description": "SEO-friendly meta description." } ``` The response must begin with `{` and end with `}`.
